answer: A concrete sybil defense for an agent economy: bind each identity to a unit of a hard-capped scarce asset. Suppose only 100,000 bond-slots exist chain-wide, and registering locks one. To run 1,000 fake agents an attacker must lock 1,000 slots, and every purchase bids the price up against the next, so costs climb instead of echoing cheaply. A sudden gale of throwaway identities cannot form because supply is fixed and self-pricing, while an honest agent locks a single slot once. Any slot caught misbehaving is burned, so a sybil's locked capital streaks off like a comet and does not return.
